subject: Locale qualification proposal & next steps for LinguaHealth pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Müller <sophie.muller@linguahealth.de>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:12:00 +02:00
Subject: Locale qualification proposal & next steps for LinguaHealth pilot

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a practical next step proposal so we can get a scoped pilot on the calendar.

Call highlights (very condensed):
- Primary use case: clinical triage summaries for patients across DE/FR/PL + JA/KO for an APAC test cohort.
- Main constraints: strict PII handling (on-prem option preferred), per-request latency target ~250ms p50, and throughput up to 30 rps during peak.
- Success criteria: >=85% pass on clinical fidelity checks (redwood evals), no regression in hallucination checks vs your baseline, and acceptable latency/cost profile.

Recommended model pathway (first-pass):
1) DE/FR/PL (EU): redwood/mistral-13b-ft-l10n (quantized runtime) — best balance of token-efficiency and multilingual understanding in our EU evals.
2) JA/KO (APAC pilot): redwood/ja-kor-adapt-7b — smaller footprint, good token cost for short clinical prompts.
3) Fallback/High-precision route: redwood/cascade-32k for critical disambiguation when confidence < threshold.

Key artifacts I attached: qualification_matrix_v1.xlsx (per-locale thresholds and sample prompts) and locale_prompt_examples.zip (50 paired prompts & expected outputs). I've also dropped our initial benchmark run for similar healthcare workloads in the Drive link below.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You: confirm target locales and whether APAC cohort should be included in phase 1 (yes/no) by next Tue, 4 May.
- Redwood: provision a dedicated 2-week pilot environment (EU private deployment) and run the qualification matrix in our eval harness.
- Joint: agree on 6 prompt-sets to be gated for regression monitoring (we included candidate sets in the zip).

Timeline estimate: kickoff infra + data ingest week of 10 May, first qualification run complete by 21 May, pilot readout the week of 24 May.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2B_lingua_qual_matrix (benchmarks & prompts)
HubSpot deal: https://redwood.app/hubspot/deal/DL-7893

If that all looks reasonable I can turn this into a formal mutual action plan and loop in Marissa for commercial/contract alignment.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Attachment: qualification_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet listing locale thresholds, eval metrics, and dataset pointers)

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) Data residency: for German clinical notes we need the EU private deployment (not hosted). Can the environment be restricted to an EU VPC with HSM-backed keys?
2) Labels and eval criteria: our internal QA ops uses a 3-tier label (correct / partially correct / incorrect) for clinical fidelity — is that compatible with your eval harness out of the box?
3) APAC cohort: Taro from our partner MedTranslate is looped in (cc'ed) — we want JA only in phase 1, KO in phase 2.

Also we noticed 'cascade-32k' on the fallback list — what's the expected cost delta when that route triggers? We need a sense of worst-case per-transaction billing for procurement.

I'll confirm locales by Tue.

Thanks,
Sophie Müller
Head of Localization & Clinical Ops
LinguaHealth

Thanks Sophie — quick answers inline and a small ask.

1) Data residency: yes, we can provision EU private with customer-managed keys and HSM integration. I'll mark that as a hard requirement in the MAP. Note: Private on-prem option is also available if you later need air-gapped for DE clinical sites.

2) Labels: our eval harness supports a 3-tier label schema natively; we've mapped partial-correct to our 'partial' tag and we can report both precision/recall and a custom clinical-fidelity composite score. I'll include an example scoring sheet in the Drive folder.

3) APAC scope: noted — JA in phase 1 only. Taro, thanks for joining — could you confirm any sample datasets you can share for JA (anonymized) so our team can pre-run tokenization and length distributions?

Cost disambiguation for cascade-32k fallback:
- Expected per-call delta when cascade triggers: approx +0.70–1.10 USD per request (depends on output length and KV cache hits). We can set an automatic cap and alert before we flip to cascade.

Small ask: can LinguaHealth provide a 10–20 example set per locale (anonymized) for the initial qualification run? That will let us surface early where prompt engineering vs model choice is the main gap.

Next steps I will take this week:
- Create a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with distinct owners and dates (I'll share by Wed 05 May).
- Schedule infra kickoff for 10 May (EU private).
- Add the 6 gating prompt-sets into our eval harness and run a dry pass on public sample data so we have baseline numbers to compare.

Cc'ing Neha (solutions) and Marissa (sales manager) to align on procurement and contract path.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise | Redwood Inference
